title: Provider consolidation risk — migration scenarios & experiment matrix
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary: Run a focused set of migration scenario experiments and produce decision artifacts that quantify the technical and commercial cost of supplier consolidation events (e.g., provider mergers, model licensing changes, sudden model deprecations). The goal is to produce concrete migration playbooks and a simulator+matrix that product, solutions, and sales can use to assess customer impact and negotiation levers.

Scope:
- Define 6 realistic consolidation event archetypes (merger, price spike, restricted license, model sunset, regional shutdown, quantization-incompatibility).
- For each archetype create migration scenarios covering small, medium, and enterprise customers (cost, latency, accuracy, SLA exposure).
- Implement 3 rapid tech experiments: multi-model A/B cost/latency comparison, quantized-compatibility probes (hosted vs dedicated), and end-to-end failover timing (region + variant fallback).
- Build a decision matrix and a migration cost calculator (spreadsheet + short-run simulator) that outputs: expected uplift in per-token cost, additional infra ops work, estimated CX tickets, and revenue-risk per customer cohort.

Why now: Market signals show increased M&A chatter among major model vendors and several license revisions in Q1 2026. Sales are asking for deterministic answers about fallback costs and contract negotiation guidance. This initiative reduces enterprise risk and helps prioritize Dedicated/Private upsell motions.
acceptance_criteria: Six consolidation archetypes documented with assumptions and data sources
Three experiments implemented end-to-end with reproducible notebooks/logs
Migration cost calculator (sheet) with knobs for region, model flavor, quantization, and traffic shape
Decision matrix and one-pager for GTM with recommended contract triggers and customer messaging
Internal runbook for technical failover (playbooks across Hosted, Dedicated, Private) reviewed by infra and SRE
tasks: Draft archetype definitions and hypothesis statements (owner: PM)
Collect vendor pricing/terms signals and repository of public notices (owner: Research)
Implement multi-model latency/cost microbenchmarks (owner: Applied ML)
Run quantization compatibility smoke tests with common hardware targets (owner: Runtime)
Simulate failover scenarios with synthetic traffic and measure recovery time (owner: SRE)
Assemble migration cost calculator and sanity-check with Solutions Eng (owner: PM + SE)
Write GTM one-pager and negotiation playbook for Enterprise Sales (owner: PM)
Review and sign-off with Legal on wording for customer-facing contract guidance (owner: Legal)
Schedule short brown-bag to share findings with Sales and CSM (owner: PM)
Create a follow-up roadmap for automation items (prefill routing policies, alerting thresholds)
notes: Edge case: some customers pin older model variants which may not have quantized equivalents — need a manual remediation path.
Preliminary research shows pricing spike scenarios can increase per-token cost by 2–8x depending on fallback model and traffic shape.
Coordinate with Legal early for guidance on customer notices and contract language for provider-driven model changes.
Keep experiment code generic so results can be replayed for other vendor events; capture seed values and env manifests.
decisions: Decision to focus initial experiments on text-generation and embeddings (not multimodal) — lowers scope and yields higher signal for Search/RAG customers.
Adopt 3 service tiers for cost-modeling: Free/SMB, Standard, Enterprise with pinned SLAs and on-call rotas.
Prioritize building the spreadsheet calculator first before investing in a full simulator; iterate to simulator after initial stakeholder reviews.
